canonical_source_of_truth: NONE. No single file/ADR today governs a general Decision concept. The closest partial authorities are: ADR-24-25-Execution-Identity-Attempt.md (constitutional; binds PromotionDecisionArtifact into the execution/promotion model) and ADR-24-21-Actor-Identity-Trust.md (constitutional; ACT-21-I10 authority-evidence binding rule) for the narrow internal-promotion-governance sense, and AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md (non-compliance-claim mapping document, explicitly not gated on the reproducible-checkpoint track) which is the only document that names the general gap (AI-GOV-3) but freezes no contract for it.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: DecisionImpactArtifact / mps-decision-governance (ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md §3)
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: This is the platform's most prominent 'Decision' vocabulary at the constitutional root (ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md lines 60-104). Examined closely and REJECTED as a reuse candidate: DecisionImpact/EvidenceSet model the extracted regulatory *knowledge content of an external legal decision document* (a beslut) for retrieval, materialized via CAS lookup -> Parse -> DecisionFacts -> DecisionImpact (MaterializationContract.ts:5). It answers 'what does this legal decision say,' never 'what choice did this system/actor make among alternatives, at what point in time, under what authority.' It is a false-friend by name, not a semantic match. Flagged as a naming SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE risk for a reviewer choosing the bare name 'DecisionImpact' or 'EvidenceSet' as if it covered the candidate's semantics -- it does not.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: PromotionDecisionArtifact (mps-promotion)
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: Closest structural match: candidate_ref (subject), evaluation_ref (evidence), governance_approval_ref (authority), decision: PROMOTE|REJECT (the choice). Rejected as full reuse: no decided_by/timestamp field at all on this interface or on the CanonicalArtifact base type it extends (mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts:54-59 has no created_at/decided_at field anywhere), so governance question 2 (point-in-time + authority) is not uniformly answerable from this representation alone. Also only models a binary accept/reject of ONE candidate, never an enumerated set of identifiable alternatives (governance question 1 fails).

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: PromotionDecisionArtifact (mps-evolution, second definition)
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: A second, non-identical interface for the same conceptual artifact: artifact_type 'PROMOTION_DECISION' (vs 'PROMOTION_DECISION_ARTIFACT' in mps-promotion), adds fitness, approved:boolean, reason, decided_by, evaluated_at that the mps-promotion variant lacks. Both 'PROMOTION_DECISION' and 'PROMOTION_DECISION_ARTIFACT' coexist as separate members of the shared ArtifactType union (mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts lines 17-18), i.e. the platform has two live, non-unified schemas for what should be one canonical decision record -- evidence against 'exactly one authoritative record' (governance question 5) and a reason ALREADY_REPRESENTED fails the lossless-reuse test.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: GovernanceApprovalArtifact / ApprovalArtifact
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: A third, again non-identical, decision-shaped artifact: governance_result: GovernanceDecision (APPROVE|REJECT|REQUEST_CHANGES), decided_by, rationale, evidence_refs, promotion_decision_ref. Rejected as sole/sufficient reuse target: it is scoped specifically to approving/rejecting a prior PromotionDecision (a decision *about* a decision), not a general-purpose 'choice among alternatives' concept, and a separate ApprovalArtifact/GovernanceArtifact hierarchy exists in contracts/ that is not reconciled with it, reinforcing the multiplicity problem.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: GovernanceReviewArtifact
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: Individual reviewer input (subject_ref, evidence_refs, reviewer, decision, comments) folded by GovernancePolicyEngine.ts:56-68 into a final GovernanceApprovalArtifact. This is reasoning-material-plus-a-vote per reviewer, closer to Evidence feeding a Decision than to the Decision itself; considered and set aside as a component, not the concept.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: ExecutionAttempt / PromotionDecisionArtifact linkage (ADR-24-25, constitutional)
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: The strongest constitutional anchor found: 'PromotionDecisionArtifact SHALL reference exactly one ExecutionAttemptArtifact' and 'SHALL reference the ExecutionOutcomeArtifact and ObservedExecutionGraphArtifact used as decision evidence' -- i.e. the ADR itself already separates Evidence (Outcome+ObservedGraph), Decision (Promotion), from what happens next (RegistryMutationArtifact), matching the candidate's own distinguishing test almost exactly. Examined as the best-fit existing constitutional pattern, but it governs promotion-of-execution-candidates specifically (internal platform self-governance), not a general kernel concept usable for an arbitrary autonomous real-world action choosing among alternatives -- confirmed by AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md's own gap note that these mechanisms govern 'governance actions on data,' not a general decision-subject artifact.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: GovernanceDecision (enum type)
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: A controlled vocabulary (APPROVE|REJECT|REQUEST_CHANGES) reused across GovernanceReviewArtifact and GovernanceApprovalArtifact. Useful raw material for a future canonical Decision type's 'chosen value' field, but is a value enum, not a governed artifact/record with identity, authority-binding, and immutability -- does not by itself satisfy any of the five governance questions.

existing_semantic_candidates_examined.name: DecisionClock
existing_semantic_candidates_examined.why_considered_and_verdict: A pure timestamp-provider interface ('now(): Date'), a mechanism utility with no semantic content about a choice. Rejected outright as irrelevant beyond a naming coincidence.

explanation:
DECISION was tested in order against the repository's actual constitutional documents and TypeScript contracts, not just against similarly-named types.

(1) WRONG_ABSTRACTION_LEVEL rejected: the platform already treats "decision" as a load-bearing normative boundary, not an implementation concern. ADR-24-21 (Actor-Identity-Trust, constitutional) ACT-21-I10 requires "Any governance decision requiring mutation authority SHALL reference exactly one AuthorityEvidenceArtifact," and packages/mps-registry/src/contracts/RegistryMutationArtifacts.ts:9-10 hard-gates state mutation on a `promotion_decision_ref` (REG-24-13-I1: "Registry SHALL NOT mutate state without a valid PromotionDecisionArtifact reference"). This is core governance plumbing, not UI/logging/backend-swap material.

(2) MECHANISM_ONLY rejected: packages/mps-governance/src/engine/GovernancePolicyEngine.ts:56-85 shows the *output* of decision logic (`governance_result`, `decided_by`, `rationale`) is itself the governed artifact, not a description of how a vote was computed. ADR-MPS-CORE-001.md:180-186 explicitly forbids re-deriving a Decision from a stale Category-C derived value, treating Decision as a distinct, non-recomputable normative fact, not a mechanism detail.

(3) ALREADY_REPRESENTED — tested via the Lossless Semantic Reuse Test below — FAILS. (4) SEMANTIC_DUPLICATE — the existing decision-shaped artifacts are not identical to each other (see schema drift below), so this class does not cleanly apply either; noted as a secondary finding. (5) DERIVABLE rejected: ADR-MPS-CORE-001.md's Trust Boundary Recalculation Rule (§5.2) explicitly forbids reusing a recomputed derived value as authorization for a new decision ("Old FitnessScore → [forbidden] → New PromotionDecision"), and EXEC-25-I3 (ADR-24-25) requires Attempt/Decision immutability after publication — i.e. the platform's own constitution requires a decision to be explicitly, immutably recorded at decision time, not reconstructed from Evidence+Outcome after the fact. (6) NOT_TECHNOLOGY_INDEPENDENT rejected: "who chose what, when, under what authority" survives any swap of the underlying selection mechanism (human review, deterministic policy engine, or an LLM), matching EXEC-25-I15 Runtime Independence already asserted for the adjacent Execution model. (7) NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_GOVERNED rejected: the concept is *already* independently instantiated as its own top-level `CanonicalArtifact` (own content_hash/identity, own artifact_type tag) in at least four separate packages (mps-core's trust-boundary example, mps-evolution, mps-promotion, mps-governance) rather than being folded as a field onto Evidence or Outcome artifacts — convergent, repeated, independent re-invention of the same shape is itself evidence that the concept needs its own lifecycle, not that it is derivable from something else's.

Having survived 1-7, disposition reaches (8) CORE_SEMANTIC_SURVIVES / TRUE_GAP — but this is a normalization-flavored true gap, not a from-nothing one: docs/architecture/AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md is the repository's own first-party admission of exactly this gap. §2 states the constitutional rule ("FINAL DECISION AUTHORITY = an explicitly identified, authorized human actor... on the artifact that constitutes the decision") and its own Gap paragraph (lines 73-79) says: "no artifact type in this codebase is yet explicitly named or typed as a legal/administrative decision subject to this rule... The mechanisms above govern governance actions on data (import, promotion, source approval), not yet an end-user-facing decision artifact." §3 independently names "observation → interpretation → decision" as an existing conceptual separation ("GENERATED != DECISION," line 98) that has never been reified as its own canonical artifact family. §9's AI-GOV-3 explicitly calls for "Decision-subject artifact typing... distinct from governance actions on data" as a still-open, unscheduled item. This is a documented, self-identified TRUE_GAP, corroborated independently by the code-level drift found below.

governance_questions_answered.explanation: Every existing decision-shaped artifact (PromotionDecisionArtifact x2, GovernanceApprovalArtifact) models a binary/tri-state gate on a single named candidate (decision: PROMOTE|REJECT, or governance_result: APPROVE|REJECT|REQUEST_CHANGES). None carries a structural field enumerating the set of identifiable alternatives that were considered; only the single subject under review is referenced (candidate_ref / subject_ref / promotion_decision_ref).
governance_questions_answered.question: What specific choice was made among identifiable alternatives?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: Answerable for the mps-evolution variant (decided_by: ActorReference, evaluated_at: string present) but NOT for the mps-promotion variant of the same conceptual artifact (packages/mps-promotion/src/contracts/PromotionDecisionArtifact.ts has no decided_by or timestamp field at all), and CanonicalArtifact, the shared base type, carries no timestamp field (mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts:54-59). The answer therefore depends on which of two non-identical schemas happened to be used, which is not a uniform, reconstructable answer.
governance_questions_answered.question: At what point in time was the choice made, and under what authority?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: evaluation_ref / evidence_refs fields are present across the promotion and governance-approval variants and reliably point at the reasoning material considered (PromotionEvaluationArtifact, GovernanceReviewArtifact refs).
governance_questions_answered.question: What material was considered in making the choice?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: Within the narrow promotion pipeline this separation is real and constitutional: ADR-24-25 EXEC-25-I10/I11 keep Evidence (Outcome + ObservedExecutionGraph), Decision (PromotionDecisionArtifact), and what-happens-next (RegistryMutationRequestArtifact/RegistryMutationExecutionArtifact) as distinct referenced artifacts.
governance_questions_answered.question: Can this exact choice be distinguished, structurally, from the reasoning material that led to it and from what happened afterward?

governance_questions_answered.explanation: No. Two non-identical PromotionDecisionArtifact interfaces coexist under two different ArtifactType tags ('PROMOTION_DECISION_ARTIFACT' and 'PROMOTION_DECISION', both listed in mps-evolution/src/core/types.ts lines 17-18) with different field sets, and a separate GovernanceApprovalArtifact/ApprovalArtifact pair shows the same pattern. Unlike mps-decision-governance's `dg-*` canonical-version namespace ownership rule (ADR-MPS-CONSTITUTIONAL-INVARIANTS.md §5, C-02), there is no equivalent single-authority freeze preventing 'Decision' identity from drifting across packages.
governance_questions_answered.question: Is there exactly one authoritative, immutable-after-the-fact record of what was chosen?

minimum_semantic_delta: A single, kernel-owned, canonically-versioned Decision artifact family (analogous in rigor to how mps-decision-governance owns the `dg-*` namespace for DecisionImpact identity) that: (1) references the full set of identifiable alternatives considered, not merely the one candidate that was chosen -- a field that exists nowhere in the repository today; (2) makes the authority binding (an ActorReference / AuthorityEvidenceArtifact reference) and the point-in-time timestamp mandatory, non-optional fields on every instance, closing the drift between the mps-promotion and mps-evolution variants; (3) references, but stays structurally distinct from, the evidence/evaluation material considered beforehand and the Outcome artifact that follows, per the separation already asserted informally in ADR-24-25 and AI-GOVERNANCE-AND-HUMAN-AUTHORITY-01.md §3 ('GENERATED != DECISION'); (4) is immutable after publication and independently content-addressed, so it can supersede -- rather than sit alongside -- the currently-duplicated PROMOTION_DECISION / PROMOTION_DECISION_ARTIFACT / GOVERNANCE_APPROVAL / GOVERNANCE_APPROVAL_ARTIFACT artifact_type variants as their common canonical ancestor. This is described only as a semantic delta, not implemented here.
